name: Dutch spyglass demonstrated
summary: In 1608 spectacle maker Hans Lipperhey presented a working spyglass in the Dutch Republic and sought a patent; printed news of it spread across Europe within weeks.
description: A working distance-magnifying spyglass presented by Hans Lipperhey and recorded in a patent request; other maker claims remain distinct.
tier_reason: A major reusable result, process or system within its field; broader multi-field or multi-generation dependence on this exact referent is not established.

date.basis: Lipperhey's demonstration and the States General record of 2 October 1608; does not date a unique invention event.

events.statement: A working distance-magnifying spyglass presented by Hans Lipperhey and recorded in a patent request; other maker claims remain distinct.
events.caveats: The record supports presentation, not exclusive inventorship; no particular later specimen is claimed to be this instrument.

evidence.locator: Rolf Willach, The long road to the invention of the telescope, printed p. 93 (PDF p. 99), opening paragraph
evidence.supports: Identifies Lipperhey's presented instrument and the dated States General entry.

date.label: November 1608
date.basis: Reeves dates Sarpi’s receipt of and reaction to the report to November 1608.

events.statement: Venetian natural philosopher Paolo Sarpi received and reacted to the circulated newsletter account of Lipperhey’s telescope by November 1608.
events.caveats: Sarpi doubted the report, which does not establish his acceptance, physical inspection or use.

evidence.locator: Eileen Reeves, printed p. 167 / PDF p. 173, first paragraph
evidence.supports: Identifies the newsletter, Lipperhey and Sarpi’s November 1608 receipt and reaction.

date.label: October–November 1608 (conflicting scholarly dates)
date.basis: In the same telescope history, Zoomers calls the newsletter early October; Zuidervaart dates its composition in October and the Paris and Lyon printed editions in November. The range preserves both assessments.

events.statement: French newsletter editions describing the Dutch telescope report circulated in print; one historian dates the Paris and Lyon editions to November 1608.
events.caveats: The historians give conflicting publication dates; this range is not a known first publication date. Publication is only an awareness proxy and proves neither acceptance nor physical use. Sarpi’s skeptical November reaction is a separate event.

evidence.locator: Huib Zuidervaart, printed p. 16 / PDF p. 22; Henk Zoomers, printed p. 301 / PDF p. 307
evidence.supports: Zuidervaart distinguishes composition in October and Paris/Lyon printing in November; Zoomers calls publication early October.

earliest_record.rationale: Earliest defensible dated record of this scoped referent in the retained evidence; later community entry is recorded separately. Reeves dates Sarpi’s receipt of and reaction to the report to November 1608. Sarpi doubted the report, which does not establish his acceptance, physical inspection or use. This is the earliest supported record currently established here, not certification of absolute priority.

community_entry.community: Readers of the Paris and Lyon printed newsletter
community_entry.rationale: Printed editions offer a documented route to public awareness; Sarpi’s skeptical response is not evidence of acceptance.
community_entry.proxy_reason: Publication supports potential exposure to readers of these editions, without proving any particular reader believed the report or used the device.
community_entry.caveats: The historians give conflicting publication dates; this range is not a known first publication date. Publication is only an awareness proxy and proves neither acceptance nor physical use. Sarpi’s skeptical November reaction is a separate event.

caveats: The record supports presentation, not exclusive inventorship; no particular later specimen is claimed to be this instrument.
